items.item: when two commits race on the same version, only one succeeds; updates verify the conditions under which they can be applied to a new version and retry if those conditions are met

CHAPTER.md's originally planned source line named 'WriteSerializable vs Serializable isolation levels' as a Delta protocol concept, but that specific naming is Databricks-proprietary (docs.databricks.com), not present in the open-source PROTOCOL.md or docs.delta.io — this topic sources Delta's open concurrency-control page instead (three-stage protocol, named exceptions) and uses Iceberg's own 'writers can select what to validate' quote for the isolation-is-a-choice idea, documented in FACT-CHECK.md's red-team #1.

at.step: Reveal: isolation is a choice, not a given

items.item: The local-disk demo models a 'delete' as a file removed from the snapshot's file list, not Iceberg's actual position/equality delete-file format — the claim is narrower: the validate-before-retry shape transfers, not the on-disk delete-file machinery, which this topic never claims to reproduce.

The two-writer race in examples.py is a scripted sequence in one process, not genuinely concurrent OS processes, same disclosed limitation as topic 12's compare-and-swap demo — what's verified is the retry logic's correctness given a real atomic CAS primitive, not a concurrency stress test.

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — append vs append, retry succeeds

items.item: Partitioning as a conflict-avoidance technique (named in docs.delta.io's write-conflicts table) is named in post-notes.md's Production section but not built in examples.py — explicitly out of scope for this topic's 20-minute budget.
This topic does not cover row-level deletes or copy-on-write vs merge-on-read — that is explicitly the next topic's subject, and this topic's own handoff names that boundary.

The prerequisites panel lists topic 12 (table-snapshot-model) as the direct dependency and Chapter 5 §5.2's optimistic/pessimistic vocabulary as declared background, matching CHAPTER.md's own stated Uses/Declared split for this topic.

Demo 1 (append vs append) and demo 2 (delete vs delete) both reuse topic 12's os.open(O_CREAT | O_EXCL) compare-and-swap primitive for the commit slot itself — this topic's new contribution is what happens after the swap, not a new atomicity primitive.

at.step: Reveal: writers stage first, validate only at commit

items.item: Iceberg's spec names compactions explicitly as an example of a replace operation that must validate its files are still present, which is why post-notes.md's Production section calls out compaction-vs-writer conflicts as a named commit-storm contributor rather than inventing that connection.

The step-8 reveal names three of Delta's five documented conflict exceptions (ConcurrentAppendException, ConcurrentDeleteReadException, ConcurrentDeleteDeleteException); MetadataChangedException and ConcurrentTransactionException/ProtocolChangedException are quoted in SOURCES.md and covered in coverage.json's source items but not individually dramatized on screen, since the reel's 10-step budget maps each exception family to the append/delete split it already built rather than enumerating all five.

at.step: Reveal: Delta names the identical distinction as typed exceptions

items.item: This topic's isolation-level claim (step 9) is deliberately narrower than CHAPTER.md's original planned framing — it says isolation is a validation choice a writer makes, sourced from Iceberg's own spec, rather than naming Delta's Databricks-specific 'WriteSerializable' level, which the open-source sources used here never document.
